headline: Approved water reserve money for design engineering of the water system on LaFountain St. and Park St.
summary: Staff described a planned water line update around the former Armory lot, which Champlain Housing Trust wants to develop. The study cost was given as between sixty and seventy-five thousand dollars, paid from a water fund reserve of a little more than $1.7 million. Residents and Champlain Housing Trust representatives shared comments before an executive session, and the request then passed 3-0 with one abstention.
decisions: Approved the November 2, 2026 meeting minutes as part of the consent agenda, 4-0.
Approved the reserve request for design engineering on the water system on LaFountain St. and Park St., 3-0 with one abstention.

Minutes: The City Manager gave an overview of the Armory project as well as an update to the status 
of Champlain Housing Trust’s partnership for developing the parcel. Collaboration with Winooski’s 
Public Works Department identified an area of opportunity for updating the water line around the 
property, and a scoping study which could be funded using the City’s water reserves, was presented to 
Council for their approval. Council has requested city staff to prioritize this project over other priorities 
currently. 
 
The Mayor recommended having an executive session followed by continued discussion and possible 
approval and allowed members of the public to share comments before entering an executive session. 
 
Jeff Myers shared their displeasure over the project’s outreach and does not believe the city should be 
fiscally responsible for any work associated with the possible development.  
 
Judy Lance asked clarifying questions about bond versus reserve spending, as well as the amount of 
the reserve request. City staff were able to answer her questions and made mention that the study’s 
cost is anywhere between sixty and up to seventy-five thousand dollars. In addition, the Finance 
Director commented that the water fund reserve balance the request is related to currently maintains 
a little more than $1.7 million. 
 
Michele Wheeler asked questions to council and staff about the necessities for upgrading the 
infrastructure as well as comparable past projects and who financed the work. 
 
Representatives from Champlain Housing Trust gave remarks that their organization is fully prepared 
to build and develop infrastructure with this project. They have presented to the City their plans, 
listened to feedback from community members, and shared their willingness to move forward with 
this proposed project. 
 
The Public Works Director spoke to members of the public and council about the sewer lines in the 
neighborhood as well as other infrastructure needs within the area that is an immediate priority to fix. 
The Public Works department will be sharing their upcoming projects for funding for next year’s 
budget soon to City Council during budget season. 
 
VII. Proposed Executive Session 
 
A. Discussion: Pursuant to 1 V.S.A. §313 (a)(1)(F), confidential attorney-client communications made 
for the purpose of providing professional legal services to the body regarding contracts with CHT 
and the National Guard as to the former Armory lot - Elaine Wang, City Manager, and Kathy Zhou, 
Paul Frank and Collins, P.C. 
 
Motion: A motion to enter into an executive session at 6:47 PM pursuant to 1 V.S.A. §313 (a)(1)(F), 
confidential attorney-client communications made for the purpose of providing professional legal 
services to the body regarding contracts with CHT and the National Guard as to the former Armory lot, 
including Elaine Wang, City Manager, Jazmine Hurley, Housing Initiative Director, Kathy Zhou, 
Attorney, Jon Rauscher, Public Works Director (if needed), and Ryan Lambert, City Engineer (if 
needed) made by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf and seconded by Councilor Turkos. Motion passed 3-0 with 
Councilor Goodrich abstaining. 
 
Motion: Motion to exit the Executive Session at 8:19 PM was made by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf and 
seconded by Councilor Ogilvie. Motion passed unanimously.

VIII. Regular Items 
 
A. Discussion/Approval: Reserve Request: Design Engineering for Water System on LaFountain St. 
and Park St. - Elaine Wang, City Manager, Jon Rauscher, Public Works Director, and Ryan Lambert, 
City Engineer 
 
Minutes: After coming out of the Executive Session, Council asked questions to city staff for further 
clarification. Councilor Ogilvie asked questions about the scope of design work and where the water 
main is focused and when, if approved, would the scoping study be complete. The City Engineer gave 
a high-level overview of previous work with the Development Review Board’s decisions regarding the 
Armory project as well as infrastructure needs around the neighborhood (there was a goal to have this 
scoping study be complete in January, with bringing the information to Council for a possible bond 
vote). The City Engineer also commented that additional survey work should be done as part of this 
study to include more of the neighborhood, which is why the price estimates for the study fluctuate.  
 
Councilor Turkos asked the Public Works Department about their roles assisting with the scoping 
study. The Public Works Department commented that they may assist with traffic coordination, 
moving manhole covers, and reviewing options to consider for next steps with the contractor. In 
addition, Councilor Turkos asked about any trade-offs required by the department as part of this new 
focus and the Public Works Director made mention that is a challenge to forecast how much 
administrative assistance will be needed at this time. The Department is currently working on drafting 
a memo with options to move forward and will be presented to Council at a later time. 
 
The Mayor asked about previous fiscal year projects that were approved which have not begun yet 
and asked if the Department of Public Works is still moving forward with those projects. Extensive 
discussion about the previously planned projects’ timeframes and grant funding requests that could 
assist in starting those projects ensued.  
 
Deputy Mayor Oakleaf asked staff to clarify what the cost request covers. The Public Works Director 
said that the cost covers the preliminary design for both working with Champlain Housing Trust and 
assists with future city project planning.  
 
Champlain Housing Trust was asked to speak with Council, which had some questions about their 
possible Armory project. As part of the proposed development project, they need information about 
what type of installation is required to connect to the water line. Additional feedback from city staff 
assisted in clarifying additional Council questions.  
 
The Mayor made remarks that while there still a lot of questions that need to be answered, they 
requested a motion for this item. 
 
Motion: Motion to approve the request as presented made by Councilor Ogilvie and seconded by 
Deputy Mayor Oakleaf. Motion passed 3-0 with Councilor Goodrich abstaining.
